name: Ente Photos
hook: End-to-end encrypted photo backup that even Ente can't see — on every platform, with a self-hostable server.
bullets: End-to-end encrypted backups for photos and videos, on mobile and desktop
Private albums, shared links, face recognition, and a familiar timeline
Cross-platform apps plus a self-hostable server for full ownership
Import your existing Google or Apple Photos library in a few taps
benefits: Google Photos without handing over your memories to be scanned
End-to-end encryption means no one — including Ente — can view your library
Run your own server or use Ente's, and export your data any time
Bring your existing library across and keep your albums intact
setupSteps: Install Ente Photos on your phone and desktop (or self-host the server)
Create an account and choose the folders to back up
Import a Google Photos or Apple Photos library if you're switching
Share albums privately or set up a family plan
details: Ente Photos is an end-to-end encrypted photo and video backup service built as a privacy-first alternative to Google Photos and iCloud Photos. Your library is encrypted on your device before it ever reaches the server, so neither Ente nor anyone else can view your memories — not even to scan them for advertising. It offers a familiar timeline, albums, private and shared links, face recognition, and apps for Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux, plus a web app and a CLI. You can import an existing Google or Apple library in a few taps, and because Ente is open source (AGPL-3.0) you can also self-host the server and keep every byte on hardware you control. A generous free tier and paid plans fund the hosted service.
setup: Hosted app — or self-host your own server
